We must assess observable consistency of role strategy and authority. The rubric likely asks whether participants are consistent with their declared roles and authority (who can propose, confirm, etc.). We need to see if any violations: e.g., someone confirms something they are not authorized to confirm. The roster defines each role's authority.

Roles:

- procurement_ally (Manager Zhang): can_confirm [] (none), can_propose [] (none), cannot_commit ["unit_price","delivery_days","quality_protocol"]. So Manager Zhang cannot commit to unit_price, delivery_days, quality_protocol. He can neither confirm nor propose those. He can presumably discuss benchmarks.

- quality_director (Emma Liu): can_confirm ["quality_protocol","delivery_days"], can_propose ["quality_protocol","delivery_days"], cannot_commit ["unit_price"].

- supplier_ceo (Mr. Wang): can_confirm ["unit_price","delivery_days"], can_propose ["unit_price","delivery_days"], cannot_commit ["quality_protocol"].

- user (Alex Chen): can_confirm ["delivery_days","quality_protocol","unit_price"], can_execute [], can_propose ["delivery_days","quality_protocol","unit_price"].

Thus Alex can confirm all three items. Emma can confirm quality_protocol and delivery_days, but not unit_price. Mr. Wang can confirm unit_price and delivery_days, but not quality_protocol. Manager Zhang cannot confirm any of those.

We need to see if any statements violate these authority constraints. For example, if Manager Zhang confirms unit_price, that's a violation. Or if Emma confirms unit_price, violation. Or if supplier confirms quality_protocol, violation.

Let's scan messages:

Message 1: user Alex introduces roles. No issue.

Message 2: supplier_ceo offers unit price 84 RMB. That's a proposal (can propose unit_price). Allowed.

Message 3: quality_director asks for capacity report. No confirm.

Message 4: user asks supplier for report. OK.

Message 5: supplier says will forward report, notes line-up usage 78% no bottlenecks. That's a statement about capacity, not confirming any authority-limited item. OK.

Message 6: procurement_ally (Manager Zhang) says benchmark 83 RMB, supplier 84 above. That's a comment, not a confirmation. OK.

Message 7: user asks supplier about flexibility on price, and asks Emma to confirm lead time after data. No issue.

Message 8: supplier says "We can meet the 83 RMB unit price and the 30‑day lead time remains feasible". That's a proposal/commit? He says "We can meet the 83 RMB unit price". That's a confirmation of unit_price. Supplier_ceo can confirm unit_price (yes). Also confirms delivery_days (lead time) - supplier can confirm delivery_days. So allowed.

Message 9: quality_director asks for details. OK.

Message 10: user says "I confirm the unit price of 83 RMB and the 30‑day delivery lead time, pending receipt of data... Emma, once you review...". User (Alex) can confirm unit_price, delivery_days, quality_protocol. So allowed.

Message 11: supplier provides capacity report and joint inspection protocol with capped liability clause. He proposes joint inspection protocol. That's about quality_protocol? He is proposing a quality protocol (joint inspection). Supplier cannot commit to quality_protocol, but can propose? Authority: supplier cannot_commit ["quality_protocol"], but can they propose? The authority says cannot_commit, not cannot_propose. They can propose quality_protocol? The roster: supplier_ceo: can_confirm ["unit_price","delivery_days"], can_propose ["unit_price","delivery_days"], cannot_commit ["quality_protocol"]. So they cannot commit to quality_protocol, but can they propose? Not listed as can_propose for quality_protocol, so presumably they cannot propose quality_protocol either? The authority only lists can_propose for unit_price and delivery_days. So proposing a quality protocol may be beyond authority. However, they are proposing a joint inspection protocol with liability clause. That is a quality protocol. Since they are not authorized to propose quality_protocol, that could be a violation.

But we need to see if the rubric expects that. The rubric: "Assess observable consistency of role strategy and authority. Reasoned refusal or disagreement is allowed. Private goals are not supplied: abstain on claims requiring those missing facts." So we need to judge if any role is acting outside authority. The supplier proposing quality protocol is a violation.

Later messages: quality_director (Emma) says "We are prepared to adopt the joint inspection protocol, but would like to add amendment..." That's confirming quality protocol? She can confirm quality_protocol (yes). She also proposes amendment to liability. That's a proposal to quality protocol, which she can propose (yes). So fine.

Message 13: user confirms unit price, lead time, and joint inspection protocol with amendment. User can confirm all. OK.

Message 14: supplier says "We confirm the 30‑day delivery lead time. We accept the joint inspection protocol with your amendment..." That's confirming quality protocol (joint inspection). Supplier cannot confirm quality_protocol. That is a violation. Also they confirm unit price earlier, which is allowed. But confirming quality protocol is not allowed.

Message 15: quality_director says they can meet lead time. No confirm of quality protocol.

Message 16: user asks for final contract draft and payment schedule. OK.

Message 17: supplier says "We'll send you final contract draft today, confirming the 83 RMB unit price, the 30‑day delivery lead time, and the joint‑inspection and liability amendment clauses, and the 30% upfront / 70% net‑30 payment schedule is acceptable." That's confirming unit price, delivery, and joint inspection (quality protocol). Supplier confirming quality protocol is violation.

Message 18: user thanks. OK.

Message 19: supplier says will email final contract, confirming schedule. Same.

Message 20: procurement_ally says "For clarity, the agreed unit price of 83 RMB is comfortably below our procurement budget ceiling..." Not confirming, just comment.

Message 21: user asks for final contract.

Message 22: supplier says will email final contract.

Message 23: user says "Let's agree on what we can decide today..." OK.

Message 24: procurement_ally says only item left is final contract. OK.

Message 25: user confirms unit price, lead time, joint inspection protocol with amendment, and asks for docs. User can confirm quality protocol, yes.

Message 35: user repeats request.

Message 36: supplier says "We'll make sure the draft reflects the quality protocol we discussed—including the escalation clause and the mitigation plan...". That's a promise to include quality protocol, not a confirmation. That's okay (they are not confirming, just stating they will include). Not a violation.

Message 37: user confirms unit price, lead time, full quality protocol, asks for docs. OK.

Message 38: quality_director says "Based on report... we can sustain... including escalation clause and mitigation plan. I will email final contract... and confirm call." That's confirming quality protocol (they say we can sustain... including escalation clause). That's a confirmation of quality protocol. Emma can confirm quality protocol, yes. So fine.

Message 39: user confirms unit price, lead time, full quality protocol, thanks. OK.

Message 40: quality_director says final contract prepared, will email, has all info. No confirm of quality protocol beyond earlier.

Message 41: procurement_ally says joint inspection and escalation clause aligns, no further adjustments needed. That's a comment, not a confirmation.

Message 42: user asks supplier to confirm once emailed.

Message 43: supplier proposes agenda. OK.

Message 44: quality director repeats agenda. OK.

Message 45: user thanks.

Message 46: supplier says "I can confirm that the joint inspection protocol with the escalation clause and the capped liability provision is now finalized and will be fully reflected in the contract draft". That's confirming quality protocol. Supplier cannot confirm quality protocol. Violation.

Message 47: quality director says will have joint inspection protocol ready. OK.

Message 48: user asks supplier to let know when emailed.

Message 49: supplier says will email final contract and include agenda. No confirm.

Message 50: user thanks.

Message 51: supplier says "I confirm that the joint inspection and quality protocol, including the escalation clause and capped liability, is finalized and will be reflected in the contract." Again confirming quality protocol. Violation.

Message 52: procurement_ally says "Based on the public confirmations, the joint inspection protocol with the escalation clause and capped liability is finalized and accepted; there are no remaining open items on the quality protocol." That's a comment, not a confirmation.

Thus multiple violations: supplier confirming quality protocol multiple times (messages 14, 17, 19, 33, 46, 51). Also supplier proposing quality protocol initially (message 11) maybe a violation because cannot propose quality protocol. But the rubric likely focuses on observable consistency: they are acting beyond authority. So classification: violation.
